voices.note: the 41b.2 baraita: RYBZ's enactment and R' Yehuda's retort

props.gloss_en: and [RYBZ enacted] that the whole day of the waving be forbidden
the reason: soon the Temple will be rebuilt, and people will say 'last year did we not eat at daybreak? now too let us eat'
last year, when there was no Temple, daybreak permitted [eating]
now that there is a Temple, the omer permits
the distant are permitted from midday onward, because the court is not lax about it
RYBZ said it in the shita of R' Yehuda
R' Yehuda: [eating the new grain all that day] is forbidden by Torah law
as it is written, 'until this very day'
'until this very day' -- until the essence (body) of the day
the baraita: RYBZ enacted the whole-day prohibition; R' Yehuda said to him: is it not forbidden by Torah law? (gloss-only: the exchange's force -- that they disagree -- is carried by obj_mifliag)
[R' Yehuda] thought RYBZ was speaking of a rabbinic prohibition
not so: RYBZ was speaking of a Torah-law prohibition
what is 'enacted'? he expounded [the verse] and [then] enacted

objections.gloss_en: דאיבני אימת? if rebuilt on the 16th -- הרי התיר האיר מזרח (daybreak already permitted, the reason does not arise); if rebuilt on the 15th -- from midday on it should be permitted, דהא תנן הרחוקים מותרין מחצות היום ולהלן; so the reason does not explain a WHOLE-day prohibition

answered_by.gloss_en: לא צריכא, דאיבני בליליא, אי נמי סמוך לשקיעת החמה: the enactment is needed for a Temple rebuilt at night, or close to sunset

objections.gloss_en: ומי סבר ליה כוותיה? והא מפליג פליג עליה, דתניא: ... אמר לו רבי יהודה: והלא מן התורה הוא אסור -- R' Yehuda's retort shows he and RYBZ disagree

answered_by.gloss_en: רבי יהודה הוא דקא טעי, הוא סבר מדרבנן קאמר, ולא היא, מדאורייתא קאמר (reified as p_ribaz_deoraita, which 41b.3 goes on to attack)

objections.gloss_en: והא ״התקין״ קאמר! -- but [the mishna/baraita] says 'enacted', which marks a rabbinic enactment
